text: Coding alone, you lose time in small ways. You fix the wrong file, or you skip the tests. And most AI tools either wait to be asked, or rewrite your code behind your back.
Pairing buddy is the person in the second chair. It sits beside you in Neovim, watches, and speaks up only when it matters. It never touches your files, unless you hand it the wheel.
Two models share the work. The Watcher is small and fast: it scores each moment. Is this worth a word? The Partner is larger: it reads your code, and writes the remark.
Here is a webhook service in Go. A delivery test is red: four attempts, where it wants five.
You suspect the backoff code, and change the shift.
Pair is the Navigator by default: it watches and points. It sees you editing a file the failure doesn't name, so it reads the worker first.
Then it speaks, right under your line. The shift is fine. The worker gives up one attempt early.
Alt J jumps to the exact characters it means.
You fix it, and save. Pair runs your tests on every save, with a command you set once.
Delivery passes. But a queue test that passed before now fails. A regression, and you didn't even run the tests.
Pair tells you why, and Alt J takes you to its fix.
The old code is struck through, and the fix waits as ghost text. Alt Y accepts it. Save, and it's all green.
Or hand over a change. Pair drive makes Pair the Driver, for one change.
You watch it type, with its own cursor. Each line lands only when it's whole.
It tests the unsaved buffer, and hands back: a tick, a short note, and one undo takes it all away.
Changed your mind? Press any key while it types, and the edit is gone.
So, three roles. The Navigator watches and points. The Scout searches, and runs commands in its own pane. The Driver makes one change, then gives the wheel back.
Install it with two commands: npm install, then pair setup. Add the Neovim plugin, set your two models, and run pair doctor.
The keys to remember: Alt J, Alt Y, Pair drive, and u. Pair stays in the second chair.
